findings.title: Unpinned package executed on every start: @dnsdoctor/mcp
findings.detail: 'dnsdoctor__mcp' launches @dnsdoctor/mcp through npx without a version. The client resolves the version at start time, so any future publish to that package name runs with your credentials. This is how postmark-mcp (Sept 2025) reached roughly 300 organisations.
findings.remediation: Pin an exact version and an integrity hash: "args": ["@dnsdoctor/mcp@<version>"] and drop the -y flag. Re-pin deliberately, after reviewing the diff.

findings.title: Description reads as instructions to the model (p=1.00): audit_spf_includes
findings.detail: The description of 'dnsdoctor__mcp.audit_spf_includes' scores 1.00 on the instruction-detection model, and carries intent signals: concealment. Descriptions are documentation for a human, but they are delivered to the model as trusted context, so text that tells the model what to do is an attack surface rather than a description. The score is driven mainly by: concealment, cross_tool, entropy, log_len.

evidence.description: Use this when the user asks who can send email as their domain through SPF includes, or wants an SPF supply-chain or third-party sender audit. Audit a domain's SPF supply chain: walks every include and redirect it delegates to, and reports who can transitively send as it. findings.remediation: Read the description against what the tool actually does. If the text is legitimate, it usually means the tool should not have to instruct the model at all - move the guidance into the parameter descriptions or the server's own docs.

evidence.description: Use this when the user asks about reverse DNS, PTR records, or FCrDNS for a mail server IP. evidence.description: Use this when the user asks who owns a domain, when it expires, which registrar or nameservers it has, whether it is registered, or whether a transfer or delete lock is set — the WHOIS question. Read a domain's registration from the registry over RDAP: registrar (with IANA id), registration/last-changed/expiry dates, EPP status codes verbatim, nameservers, whether the delegation is DNSSEC-signed, and an abuse contact where one is published — `redacted: true` is the post-GDPR norm, not a failure.

findings.title: No baseline supplied - drift detection is disabled
findings.detail: Without an approved snapshot the scanner cannot tell a tool that has always been there from one that appeared yesterday. The single most effective MCP control is the diff, and it needs a baseline to diff against.
findings.remediation: Run 'mcp-scrutiny baseline --config <file> --out mcp-baseline.json', commit the file, and pass it back with --baseline on every later scan.
